# Juicebox.ai — Style Reference

> Graph-paper dossier in a ruled margin, stamped in plum ink. Roobert headlines and typewritten DM Mono caps sit on white stock framed by 1px pewter rules, with a single plum ink saved for badges and the dithered band.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Juicebox runs a typewritten-blueprint product language. Content is set in grotesks, while every word you click or scan as a label is typed in DM Mono 500 uppercase. The canvas is a two-tone paper stack: #f8f6f8 Mist Canvas outside a column ruled in 1px #786c78, #ffffff Paper Canvas inside it, and #edf2f0 Sage Surface for feature bays. The chromatic budget is exactly one hue. Plum #6a2f8d and its tints appear only in the hero badge, link text and the dithered gradient band, while the primary CTA stays near-black #2a232a. Roobert at weight 500 carries headlines up to 64px with -0.02em tracking that tightens to -0.04em at display size. Neue Haas Grotesk Text 400 handles prose, and DM Mono owns 73 label instances, more than any other family. Shapes are nearly sharp: 2px and 4px account for 76 of 105 measured radii. Depth comes from rules and tonal shifts rather than shadows. The page reads as an engineer's annotated spec sheet rather than a glossy SaaS landing page.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper Canvas | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-canvas` | Inner content column, hero frame, secondary button fill and product demo window (59 background uses) — this is the sheet the whole spec is drawn on. |
| Mist Canvas | `#f8f6f8` | `--color-mist-canvas` | Outer page ground beyond the ruled column, nav backdrop and quiet secondary panels (23 uses) — its faint mauve cast ties every neutral back to the plum accent. |
| Sage Surface | `#edf2f0` | `--color-sage-surface` | Feature bays below the demo band and long showcase panels (8 uses) — a cool green-grey tonal step that separates sections without a single shadow. |
| Carbon Ink | `#1d161d` | `--color-carbon-ink` | Every h1, h2 and h3, plus emphasized phrases in the hero lead (37 uses) — a plum-tinted near-black that reads warmer and softer than pure black. |
| Graphite Caption | `#574e57` | `--color-graphite-caption` | Nav labels, mono eyebrows, input text and body paragraphs (49 uses, with the near-duplicate #564e56 merged in rather than kept as a token) — the workhorse reading tone. |
| Pewter Line | `#786c78` | `--color-pewter-line` | The 1px column frame, nav underline, dashed outer rails and tertiary meta text (7 uses) — it draws the blueprint. Do not use it for paragraph copy. |
| Ash Caption | `#a89ea8` | `--color-ash-caption` | Placeholder text, disabled labels, small metadata and neutral dither pixels (13 uses) — the faintest legible tone, reserved for things the eye may skip. |
| Cream Ink | `#faf9fa` | `--color-cream-ink` | Text on the Jet Fill CTA, mono labels on dark chips and the plum band (32 uses) — an off-white that keeps inverted type from glaring. |
| Concrete Rule | `#eeecee` | `--color-concrete-rule` | Hairline dividers drawn as 1px fills, logo-strip cell rules and the secondary button ring (45 uses) — structure without weight. |
| Jet Fill | `#2a232a` | `--color-jet-fill` | The primary "Try for free" button and dark label chips (6 uses) — the only filled action color. Do not swap it for plum. |
| Plum Signal | `#6a2f8d` | `--color-plum-signal` | Badge text and border, link color and the base of the dithered band (6 uses across fill and text) — the single hue in the system. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Lilac Wash | `#f1e6f8` | `--color-lilac-wash` | Announcement badge fill and hero dither tint (7 uses) — plum at whisper strength, and the only place the accent touches a light surface. |
| Orchid Pulse | `#b054e7` | `--color-orchid-pulse` | Brightest pixels in the dithered band and gradient highlights (1 use) — decorative-only. Do not use it for text, borders or buttons. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Roobert — the quiet-weight display face for every section headline · `--font-roobert`
- **Substitute:** Space Grotesk at 500 (closest skeleton, slightly quirkier terminals), Inter Tight at 500, Plus Jakarta Sans at 500. Roobert Medium draws true to its nominal weight, so match 500 with 500 and do not reach for 600.
- **Weights:** 500
- **Sizes:** 12px, 28px, 40px, 48px, 64px
- **Line height:** 1.33 at 12px, 1.25 at 28px, 1.15 at 40px, 1.0 at 48px, 1.0 at 64px
- **Letter spacing:** 0px at 12px, -0.56px at 28px, -0.8px at 40px, -0.96px at 48px, -2.56px at 64px
- **Role:** Weight 500 at display sizes is the signature. Headlines are large but not shouting, where the SaaS convention is 600 to 700. Tracking holds at -0.02em through 48px and then doubles to -0.04em at 64px, so the single h1 locks into a dense slab. The 48px-to-64px step is a Perfect Fourth (1.333), while the lower steps run looser, so hierarchy comes from size alone and weight stays fixed.

### Neue Haas Grotesk Text — the neutral prose voice for leads, body and fine print · `--font-neue-haas-grotesk-text`
- **Substitute:** Arimo at 400 (metric-compatible Helvetica skeleton), Inter at 400 (draws slightly wider, so keep the -0.01em tracking), Public Sans at 400. Haas Grot Text 55 Roman renders with a sturdy text-cut stroke, so avoid 300-weight substitutes that will read thin.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 14px, 16px, 18px, 20px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.08, 1.2, 1.25, 1.29, 1.33, 1.5
- **Letter spacing:** -0.24px at 12px, -0.14px at 14px, -0.42px at 14px for compact UI, -0.16px at 16px, -0.18px at 18px, -0.2px at 20px for the hero lead, -0.4px at 20px for subheads
- **Role:** This is the text cut of the Helvetica lineage, chosen for paragraphs rather than display, and it stays at 400 so Roobert and DM Mono can own emphasis. Sizes step in flat 2px increments, a ratio of roughly 1.125, which is gentler than a Minor Third and keeps reading text uniform. Weight 700 appears only 4 times, all inside the 20px hero lead to bold the product name.

### DM Mono — the typewritten interface voice for every label and action · `--font-dm-mono`
- **Substitute:** DM Mono at 500 (open-source, so use the original), IBM Plex Mono at 500, JetBrains Mono at 500. DM Mono 500 renders medium-firm, so 400 substitutes read noticeably weaker against the grotesk.
- **Weights:** 500
- **Sizes:** 13px, 14px, 15px
- **Line height:** 1.0 at 13px, 1.14 at 14px, 1.0 at 15px
- **Letter spacing:** 1px at 13px (button labels), 0.28px at 14px (nav and eyebrows), 0.3px at 15px (stat labels)
- **Role:** With 73 instances, the most-used family on the page, mono uppercase is the interface itself rather than a code accent. Nav links, buttons, eyebrows, badges and logo-strip captions are all typed. Positive tracking of 0.02em, widened to 0.077em on 13px button labels, opens the caps into stamped labels, the anti-convention to the sentence-case sans nav most SaaS sites ship.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Neue Haas Grotesk Text | 400 | 12px | 1.0 | -0.24px | `--text-small` |
| caption | DM Mono | 500 | 13px | 1.0 | 1px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | DM Mono | 500 | 14px | 1.14 | 0.28px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Neue Haas Grotesk Text | 400 | 16px | 1.25 | -0.16px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Neue Haas Grotesk Text | 400 | 18px | 1.33 | -0.18px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Neue Haas Grotesk Text | 400 | 20px | 1.25 | -0.4px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Roobert | 500 | 28px | 1.25 | -0.56px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Roobert | 500 | 40px | 1.15 | -0.8px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Roobert | 500 | 48px | 1.0 | -0.96px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Roobert | 500 | 64px | 1.0 | -2.56px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Set every navigational, button and eyebrow word in DM Mono 500 uppercase, at 0.28px tracking for 14px and 1px for 13px — the typewritten label voice is the system's one defining move.
- Keep all Roobert headlines at weight 500 and track them -0.02em, tightening to -2.56px only at the 64px display — size carries hierarchy and weight stays constant.
- Fill the primary CTA with #2a232a and #faf9fa text at 4px radius — near-black keeps the action legible without spending the plum.
- Draw structure with 1px #786c78 frames and #eeecee dividers — rules replace shadows as the main separator.
- Separate sections with tonal surfaces (#ffffff, then #f8f6f8, then #edf2f0) and 160px gaps — depth is read through tone, not blur.
- Confine plum #6a2f8d to the badge, links and the dithered band, and treat that one hue as non-negotiable — scarcity is what makes the badge register.
- Use 2px radius for tags and small tiles and 4px for buttons — corners stay drafted, not friendly.

### Don't
- Don't set nav links or buttons in sentence-case Neue Haas Grotesk Text at 14px — the page loses its typewritten voice and collapses into generic SaaS.
- Don't bold headlines to 700 at 48px — the restraint of weight 500 is the authority, and heavier weights turn spec-sheet calm into marketing volume.
- Don't fill the primary button with #6a2f8d — once plum becomes the CTA, the badge and band stop being special and the one-hue budget is spent twice.
- Don't round cards to 12px or buttons to 8px as SaaS convention suggests — 16px belongs only to the demo window, and spreading it erases the outlier.
- Don't add `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 4px 4px 0px` shadows to every panel — elevation is reserved for the product window, and shadowed sections contradict the ruled-paper logic.
- Don't introduce a second saturated hue such as #186bd8 outside the product mockup — blue and teal are mockup-internal and never system accents.
- Don't tighten DM Mono tracking to -0.14px to match the grotesk — negative tracking on mono caps crushes the stamped-label rhythm.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- page ground: #f8f6f8 (Mist Canvas)
- headline text: #1d161d (Carbon Ink)
- body and label text: #574e57 (Graphite Caption)
- rules and frame: #786c78 (Pewter Line)
- accent: #6a2f8d (Plum Signal)
- primary action: #2a232a (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and bars run in #574e57 and #a89ea8 neutrals on #ffffff, with a single highlighted series in #6a2f8d and comparison fills in #f1e6f8, so plum marks the one answer instead of coloring every series.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button labeled "TRY FOR FREE": background #2a232a, text #faf9fa, no border, border-radius 4px, padding 13px 14px, rendered height 42px, font DM Mono weight 500 at 13px, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing 1px, text-transform uppercase, no shadow. Place a secondary "BOOK A DEMO" button beside it at a 10px gap, using background #ffffff, text #1d161d, a 1px solid #eeecee border, the same 4px radius, padding, font and tracking.

2. Build a hero section inside a #ffffff column with a 1px solid #786c78 left and right border, max-width 1440px, on a #f8f6f8 page. Center the stack with 160px top padding. Start with a badge: background #f1e6f8, 1px solid #6a2f8d border, radius 2px, padding 4px 8px, DM Mono 500 13px uppercase, letter-spacing 1px, color #6a2f8d, text "TRY OUR ALL-NEW AGENTS →". Leave a 24px gap, then an h1 in Roobert 500 at 64px, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -2.56px, color #1d161d. Leave a 24px gap, then a 20px Neue Haas Grotesk Text 400 lead, line-height 1.25, letter-spacing -0.2px, color #1d161d, max-width 700px, with the product name at weight 700. Leave a 32px gap, then the button pair from prompt 1. Add a lilac pixel-dither background rising from the bottom corners using #f1e6f8 and #a89ea8 squares.

3. Build a navigation bar 64px tall with background #f8f6f8, a 1px solid #786c78 bottom border and no shadow. Put the wordmark left, followed by links FEATURES, AGENTS, PRICING, RESOURCES and COMPANY at a 24px gap, in DM Mono 500 at 14px, line-height 1.14, letter-spacing 0.28px, uppercase, color #574e57, with small chevrons on menu items. On the right, at a 12px gap, place "SIGN IN" and "BOOK A DEMO" as text-only ghost buttons in #1d161d, then a "TRY FOR FREE" button with #2a232a fill, #faf9fa text, 4px radius and 13px 14px padding.

4. Build a product demo window: a full-bleed band with a background that shades from deep plum to #6a2f8d, with #b054e7 dither pixels at the edges and 160px top padding. Center a chip over it with background #2a232a, color #faf9fa, DM Mono 500 14px uppercase, 0.28px tracking, radius 2px and padding 4px 8px, reading "TRY IT OUT OR SCROLL DOWN". Leave a 16px gap, then add a #ffffff card with 16px top radius, 32px padding and box-shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 2px 4px 0px, rgba(76, 76, 76, 0.2) 0px 0px 10px 0px`. Inside it, place a borderless transparent textarea in Neue Haas Grotesk Text 400 at 14px with #574e57 text and #a89ea8 placeholder.

5. Build a three-cell proof strip on #ffffff: three equal columns separated by 1px #eeecee rules, each with 16px padding. Head each cell with a DM Mono 500 14px uppercase stat in #574e57, letter-spacing 0.28px, such as "80+ PUBLIC ENTERPRISES". Place a horizontally scrolling row of 25px-tall customer logos 16px beneath it, with a 32px gap between logos.

**Role:** The single filled call to action

Square-shouldered and inked. The button uses #2a232a background, #faf9fa text, no border, 4px border-radius, 13px 14px padding and 42px height, with DM Mono at 13px weight 500, uppercase, 1px tracking and no shadow. Despite the inherited component name it is not a pill, and the 4px corner keeps it in the drafting-table vocabulary. Using near-black where convention spends the brand hue on the CTA means the action wins on contrast, not color.

### Paper Button — Ringed (Secondary)
**Role:** The quieter companion action, "Book a Demo"

A white tab beside the ink. The button uses #ffffff background, #1d161d text, a 1px #eeecee ring, 4px border-radius, 13px 14px padding and 42px height, with DM Mono at 13px weight 500, uppercase, 1px tracking and no shadow. It pairs with the Jet Fill button at a 10px gap in the hero and reads as an alternative route rather than a demoted one.

### Ghost Button — Nav and Dark Band
**Role:** Text-only action on any surface

The lightest action tier. It has a transparent background in the nav and a #ffffff1a translucent overlay on dark bands (an overlay, not a system token), with #1d161d text on light or #faf9fa on dark, no border, 4px border-radius and 13px 14px padding, set in DM Mono at 13px weight 500 uppercase with 1px tracking. Use it for "Sign in" and repeated "Book a Demo" links, so a cluster of three actions never turns into three boxes.

### Ruled Navigation Bar
**Role:** Persistent top index of mono links

A typed table of contents. The bar sits on #f8f6f8 at 64px height (estimated) with a 1px #786c78 bottom rule, 0px radius and no shadow. The wordmark sits left, followed by FEATURES, AGENTS, PRICING, RESOURCES and COMPANY in DM Mono at 14px weight 500 with 0.28px tracking in #574e57, with small chevrons on menus. Sign In, a ghost Book a Demo and the Jet Fill Try for Free button sit right at a 12px gap. It reads as a document header rather than an app chrome bar.

### Announcement Badge — Plum
**Role:** Launch callout above the hero headline

The one plum stamp. The badge uses #f1e6f8 fill, #6a2f8d text, a 1px #6a2f8d border, 2px radius and 4px 8px padding, with DM Mono at 13px weight 500, uppercase, 1px tracking and a trailing arrow. It is the only place the accent appears at full strength on a light surface, which is why it draws the eye before the 64px headline does.

### Dithered Hero Panel
**Role:** Opening statement inside the ruled column

A pixel-field poster. The panel is a #ffffff frame with a lilac dither of #f1e6f8 and #a89ea8 pixels rising from the lower corners. It stacks the badge, a Roobert 64px weight 500 headline in #1d161d at -2.56px tracking, a 20px Neue Haas Grotesk Text lead in #1d161d with the product name at 700, and the button pair, all centered with 24px gaps. The dither swaps a gradient's gloss for a printed, bitmap texture.

### Proof Logo Strip — Three Cells
**Role:** Social proof grouped by segment

A segmented ledger. Three equal cells are divided by 1px #eeecee rules on #ffffff, each headed by a DM Mono 14px weight 500 uppercase stat in #574e57 such as "64% of the Forbes AI 50", above a horizontally scrolling marquee of customer logos about 25px tall. The logos keep their own brand colors, which are decorative and not system tokens. Splitting proof into labeled columns turns a logo wall into an annotated table.

### Product Demo Window (Main Content Card)
**Role:** Interactive product preview, the hero object

The system outlier. The card is #ffffff with a 16px top radius and the md shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 2px 4px 0px, rgba(76, 76, 76, 0.2) 0px 0px 10px 0px`. It has 32px internal padding and sits centered inside the plum band beneath a "Try it out or scroll down" chip. It breaks both the 4px shape ceiling and the shadowless rule on purpose, because it is the only thing on the page that is meant to look like real software.

### Natural-Language Search Input
**Role:** Prompt field inside the demo

Bare and unboxed. A 668px textarea with transparent background, #574e57 text, no border, 0px radius and 0px padding, set in Neue Haas Grotesk Text at 14px weight 400 with 1.2 line height and #a89ea8 placeholder text. The containing window supplies the frame, so the field reads as a sentence you type rather than a form you fill.

### Dark Mono Chip
**Role:** Instructional label on dark surfaces

A typed tab on plum. The chip has #2a232a fill, #faf9fa text, 2px radius and 4px 8px padding, set in DM Mono at 14px weight 500, uppercase, with 0.28px tracking. Its single use is "Try it out or scroll down" above the demo window. It is a Jet Fill chip rather than a plum chip so the band keeps one hue.

### Plum Dither Band
**Role:** Full-bleed stage for the demo

The chromatic peak. The band is a full-width section that shades from deep plum into #6a2f8d, with #b054e7 dither pixels at its brightest edges, 160px top padding and no radius. It hosts the demo window, which overlaps the band's lower edge. It is the only saturated area on the page, and it spends the entire color budget in one place.

### Hatched Section Divider
**Role:** Transition into Sage feature bays

Drafting-film seam. A strip about 24px tall of diagonal #eeecee hatching on #f8f6f8 sits between the demo zone and the #edf2f0 Sage Surface. It is followed by feature blocks with Roobert 40px weight 500 headings and DM Mono eyebrows. The hatch marks a cut line on a technical drawing, a section break that needs neither shadow nor color.

### Blueprint Column Frame
**Role:** Page-wide structural ruling

The scaffolding made visible. A 1px solid #786c78 rule bounds the white content column, with a second 1px dashed #786c78 rail 10px outside it, both running the full page height over the #f8f6f8 ground. A folded-corner ornament at the hero's top-right reinforces the paper metaphor. Exposing the grid lines is anti-convention, since most sites hide their columns.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do
- Set every navigational, button and eyebrow word in DM Mono 500 uppercase, at 0.28px tracking for 14px and 1px for 13px — the typewritten label voice is the system's one defining move.
- Keep all Roobert headlines at weight 500 and track them -0.02em, tightening to -2.56px only at the 64px display — size carries hierarchy and weight stays constant.
- Fill the primary CTA with #2a232a and #faf9fa text at 4px radius — near-black keeps the action legible without spending the plum.
- Draw structure with 1px #786c78 frames and #eeecee dividers — rules replace shadows as the main separator.
- Separate sections with tonal surfaces (#ffffff, then #f8f6f8, then #edf2f0) and 160px gaps — depth is read through tone, not blur.
- Confine plum #6a2f8d to the badge, links and the dithered band, and treat that one hue as non-negotiable — scarcity is what makes the badge register.
- Use 2px radius for tags and small tiles and 4px for buttons — corners stay drafted, not friendly.

### Don't
- Don't set nav links or buttons in sentence-case Neue Haas Grotesk Text at 14px — the page loses its typewritten voice and collapses into generic SaaS.
- Don't bold headlines to 700 at 48px — the restraint of weight 500 is the authority, and heavier weights turn spec-sheet calm into marketing volume.
- Don't fill the primary button with #6a2f8d — once plum becomes the CTA, the badge and band stop being special and the one-hue budget is spent twice.
- Don't round cards to 12px or buttons to 8px as SaaS convention suggests — 16px belongs only to the demo window, and spreading it erases the outlier.
- Don't add `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 4px 4px 0px` shadows to every panel — elevation is reserved for the product window, and shadowed sections contradict the ruled-paper logic.
- Don't introduce a second saturated hue such as #186bd8 outside the product mockup — blue and teal are mockup-internal and never system accents.
- Don't tighten DM Mono tracking to -0.14px to match the grotesk — negative tracking on mono caps crushes the stamped-label rhythm.

| 0 | Mist Canvas | `#f8f6f8` | Outer page ground and nav backdrop behind the ruled column |

## Elevation

Shadows are rare, with 11 instances across the whole page, and each one is functional rather than atmospheric. Ruled lines and tonal surface steps do the everyday separating.

- **Product demo window:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 2px 4px 0px, rgba(76, 76, 76, 0.2) 0px 0px 10px 0px`
- **Floating mockup cards inside the demo:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 4px 4px 0px`
- **Inset pixel tiles in the dithered band:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5) 0px 0px 12px 0px inset`
- **Small UI chips in product screens:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 1px 2px -1px, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) 0px 1px 3px 0px`
- **Side drawer edge in the mockup:** `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1) -9.5px 0px 19px 0px`

## Imagery

Imagery is almost entirely product interface: an interactive demo window, a 1406px-wide product screenshot with 0px radius, and customer logos. There is no photography and no character illustration. Screens sit inside the #ffffff demo window at 16px radius with the md shadow, or flush and unframed within the ruled column. Customer logos keep their native colors at about 25px tall and run in a marquee, so they act as decorative content rather than system tokens. Icons are small line chevrons and arrows drawn at text weight. The signature texture is a bitmap dither: lilac pixels rising in the hero, and plum-to-#b054e7 pixels across the band. This is a decorative treatment, not a gradient token, and it replaces the usual glowing orb with a printed, low-resolution grain. Overall, the imagery tells a story of software rendered on drafting paper.

## Layout

The page sits in a 1440px maximum frame with 1280px content and 700px-wide hero text. Everything lives inside a white column bounded by a solid 1px rule and a dashed outer rail over the #f8f6f8 ground. Sections stack at a 160px rhythm. The hero centers the badge, a 64px headline, the lead and the button pair over a dither field. A three-cell proof strip follows, then the full-bleed plum band with the overlapping demo window, then hatched dividers into #edf2f0 feature bays that alternate text with screens. Features run in two columns with 576px text blocks, and the proof row runs in three. The nav is 64px, filled with #f8f6f8 and ruled underneath, with the wordmark and mono links left and three actions right. At 375px, drop the display headline to 40px and the section gap to 64px, and stack the button pair. The density is comfortable.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #ffffff (Paper Canvas)
- page ground: #f8f6f8 (Mist Canvas)
- headline text: #1d161d (Carbon Ink)
- body and label text: #574e57 (Graphite Caption)
- rules and frame: #786c78 (Pewter Line)
- accent: #6a2f8d (Plum Signal)
- primary action: #2a232a (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts and bars run in #574e57 and #a89ea8 neutrals on #ffffff, with a single highlighted series in #6a2f8d and comparison fills in #f1e6f8, so plum marks the one answer instead of coloring every series.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button labeled "TRY FOR FREE": background #2a232a, text #faf9fa, no border, border-radius 4px, padding 13px 14px, rendered height 42px, font DM Mono weight 500 at 13px, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing 1px, text-transform uppercase, no shadow. Place a secondary "BOOK A DEMO" button beside it at a 10px gap, using background #ffffff, text #1d161d, a 1px solid #eeecee border, the same 4px radius, padding, font and tracking.

2. Build a hero section inside a #ffffff column with a 1px solid #786c78 left and right border, max-width 1440px, on a #f8f6f8 page. Center the stack with 160px top padding. Start with a badge: background #f1e6f8, 1px solid #6a2f8d border, radius 2px, padding 4px 8px, DM Mono 500 13px uppercase, letter-spacing 1px, color #6a2f8d, text "TRY OUR ALL-NEW AGENTS →". Leave a 24px gap, then an h1 in Roobert 500 at 64px, line-height 1.0, letter-spacing -2.56px, color #1d161d. Leave a 24px gap, then a 20px Neue Haas Grotesk Text 400 lead, line-height 1.25, letter-spacing -0.2px, color #1d161d, max-width 700px, with the product name at weight 700. Leave a 32px gap, then the button pair from prompt 1. Add a lilac pixel-dither background rising from the bottom corners using #f1e6f8 and #a89ea8 squares.

3. Build a navigation bar 64px tall with background #f8f6f8, a 1px solid #786c78 bottom border and no shadow. Put the wordmark left, followed by links FEATURES, AGENTS, PRICING, RESOURCES and COMPANY at a 24px gap, in DM Mono 500 at 14px, line-height 1.14, letter-spacing 0.28px, uppercase, color #574e57, with small chevrons on menu items. On the right, at a 12px gap, place "SIGN IN" and "BOOK A DEMO" as text-only ghost buttons in #1d161d, then a "TRY FOR FREE" button with #2a232a fill, #faf9fa text, 4px radius and 13px 14px padding.

4. Build a product demo window: a full-bleed band with a background that shades from deep plum to #6a2f8d, with #b054e7 dither pixels at the edges and 160px top padding. Center a chip over it with background #2a232a, color #faf9fa, DM Mono 500 14px uppercase, 0.28px tracking, radius 2px and padding 4px 8px, reading "TRY IT OUT OR SCROLL DOWN". Leave a 16px gap, then add a #ffffff card with 16px top radius, 32px padding and box-shadow `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05) 0px 2px 4px 0px, rgba(76, 76, 76, 0.2) 0px 0px 10px 0px`. Inside it, place a borderless transparent textarea in Neue Haas Grotesk Text 400 at 14px with #574e57 text and #a89ea8 placeholder.

5. Build a three-cell proof strip on #ffffff: three equal columns separated by 1px #eeecee rules, each with 16px padding. Head each cell with a DM Mono 500 14px uppercase stat in #574e57, letter-spacing 0.28px, such as "80+ PUBLIC ENTERPRISES". Place a horizontally scrolling row of 25px-tall customer logos 16px beneath it, with a 32px gap between logos.

## Typewritten Labeling

The discipline is that every word with a job, whether it navigates, triggers or classifies, is typed in DM Mono 500 uppercase with positive tracking: 0.28px at 14px and 1px at 13px. Prose and headlines never take that voice. This produces two clear registers, typed instructions and set content, and the thesis lives in that split. It breaks the moment a button label slips into Neue Haas Grotesk Text, a paragraph is set in mono, or mono caps receive negative tracking. To extend the system, decide first whether a new element is an instruction or content. Tabs, filters, table headers, form labels and status chips are instructions and become DM Mono 14px. Tooltips and descriptions are content and use the grotesk at 14px with -0.14px tracking.

## Rationed Plum

The chromatic budget is one hue, and it is spent in exactly three places: the #f1e6f8 badge with its #6a2f8d text, link color, and the dithered band peaking at #b054e7. Keeping the CTA in #2a232a rather than brand color is non-negotiable, because it lets the plum act as punctuation rather than decoration. The budget breaks when plum fills buttons, tints card backgrounds or appears as icon color in feature lists. It also breaks when the mockup's #186bd8 blue or #2f878d teal (both mockup-internal) leaks into marketing UI. To extend it, add plum only as a 10% tint for selected states, or as a single highlighted chart series, and keep every new surface neutral.

## Blueprint Ruling

Structure is drawn, not lifted. A 1px #786c78 solid frame, a dashed outer rail, #eeecee cell dividers and diagonal hatch strips do the work that drop shadows and rounded cards do on conventional SaaS pages. Only 11 shadows exist on a page more than 126,000px tall. The ruling breaks when panels gain 12px radii and soft shadows, when the frame lines are removed for a full-bleed modern look, or when dividers thicken to 2px. To extend it, put new modules inside the ruled column, split grids with 1px #eeecee lines, and change surface by tone (#ffffff, #f8f6f8, #edf2f0). Shadows stay reserved for objects that represent live software, such as the demo window.

## Similar Brands

- **Vercel** — Pairs a grotesk display with mono uppercase labels and hairline-ruled grids on a near-white canvas, though Vercel stays strictly monochrome where Juicebox spends one plum hue.
- **PlanetScale** — Uses mono-heavy interface labels, sharp 2px to 4px corners and visible grid lines as its main structure, in a darker, more developer-facing palette.
- **Ashby** — A direct recruiting-software competitor on a neutral canvas with product-screenshot storytelling, but with friendlier rounded cards and sentence-case UI labels.
- **Supabase** — Sets section eyebrows in tracked mono caps and confines a single saturated brand hue to accents, with a dark default theme where Juicebox is light.
- **Linear** — Holds headlines at a medium weight with tight negative tracking and lets product screenshots carry the page, though it leans on glow gradients rather than bitmap dither.
